title: 第7章 选择御兽
novel_title: 御兽仙朝：我能设计进化形态
content_zh:
出了教室，过连廊往左，人就一点点多了起来。

    罗影本以为，顶天也就是教室里那五百号人一道往前走。

    可拐过连廊尽头那道月洞门，眼前豁然一开，他脚下的步子不由得顿了一顿。

    人。

    满眼都是人。

    一股一股的少年从四面八方的教室里涌出来，往广场上汇。

    像是开春化雪的时节，几条小溪一齐灌进了同一道河床。

    罗影那一间教室的五百人落进这片人海里，连点水花都没溅起来。

    他粗粗扫了一圈，在心里估了个数。

    少说，也有五千。

    有穿锦缎的，身后跟着捧匣子的仆从。

    有穿粗布的，肩上搭着打了补丁的包袱。

    有十四五岁、脸还带着稚气的，也有二十出头、下巴上冒了胡茬的。

    从五湖四海到三教九流，今天都挤到了这个广场上。

    广场前面，有十个左右穿青色长袍的师兄，他们正忙于维护现场秩序。

    那袍子比金教习的还讲究些，是上好的细布，左胸前都绣着一片小小的叶子，针脚细密，连叶脉都根根分明。

    为首的师兄大概十六七岁的样子，望着下方乌泱泱的人头，低声道：

    “今年又是五千多号人。”

    身边年纪稍微大一点的师兄“嗯”了一声，并没有放在心上。

    这样的情况他已经见过三次了，每年春天都是这样的情景。

    进门的时候有五千张面孔，半年后能留下的已经不够五百人了。

    他瞥了瞥人群中那些缩着脖子、捂着旧包袱的人，又看了看那些仆从前呼后拥的人...

    心里那点说不清的滋味一闪而过。

    谁才是泥鳅，谁才是龙？

    这个时候看不出来。

    每个师兄的肩上，都有一只鹦鹉。

    鹦鹉比一般的【叫卖鹦】要大得多。

    全身羽毛为鲜亮的孔雀蓝，尾羽拖得很长。

    在喙边还描着一圈细细的金纹，太阳一照，就会发出光来。

    为首那师兄并不高声。

    他只是淡淡地说了一句“东边，三十排往里站”，但是这句话却突然扩大了十倍，清楚地传到了广场上每一个角落。

    最有趣的是，几千个人头挤在了一起...

    按照正常情况来说，应该是闹得沸沸扬扬如同赶集一样。

    但是那片嗡嗡的人声却在此时，被压制得很低，衬得师兄那一句话更加清楚。

    罗影认识这种鸟。

    【喧市鹦】，【叫卖鹦】的进化体。

    去年去集市的时候，他在镇上最大的兽材行前见过一只。

    那时候那只鸟站在掌柜的肩头，扯着嗓子叫卖，整条街上都能听到它的叫声。

    罗影在远处看了半晌，听见旁边卖菜的老汉嘀咕，说：

    “这鸟金贵得很，便是觉醒等级再低的，也得十几两银子。”

    一般的庄稼人是不敢想的，所以只有大商号才愿意养一只来摆阔气。

    十几两。

    罗影不自觉地摸了摸自己的衣袖。

    袖子里面什么也没有，非常空旷。

    但是他还觉得那个地方很沉。

    老黑的那对角，总共是六两。

    一头牛喂了十五年，半夜里在石柱上撞了不知多少回，才从自个儿脑袋上卸下来的东西，六两。

    而这广场上，单是师兄肩头这一只鸟，就抵得过老黑那对角，还得富余出小半截。

    这样的鸟，这里立着十来只。

    就为了让人排队。

    罗影没有眼红，也红不起来。

    他只是觉得，自己脚下这块青砖，和那些师兄脚下的青砖，明明是同一片广场，中间却像是隔着一条看不见的河。

    师兄们指挥着人流，一排一排地往广场尽头那座阁子里送。

    那阁子却不大。

    青砖砌的墙，黛瓦覆的顶，门脸还没书院正门气派，搁在这么大的广场上，倒显得有些不起眼。

    罗影心里直犯嘀咕。

    这么座寻常大小的阁子，五千号人，怎么挤得进去？

    可前头的人一排排走进去，就跟泥牛入海一般，进去多少，里头便不声不响地装下多少，门口竟不见半分拥堵。

    轮到罗影这一排了。

    李子诚挨在他身边，两人肩膀贴着肩膀，随着人流往门里挪。

    “挨紧些。”

    李子诚压低了声音：

    “人多，别冲散了。”
content_en:
After leaving the classroom, crossing the corridor to the left, there were more and more people.

Luo Ying originally thought that Dingtian was the five hundred people in the classroom walking forward together.

But after turning around the moon cave door at the end of the corridor, his eyes suddenly opened, and he couldn't help but pause in his steps.

people.

There are people everywhere.

A stream of young people poured out from the classrooms in all directions and converged on the square.

Like the beginning of spring when the snow melts, several small streams flow into the same river bed.

The five hundred people in Luo Ying's classroom fell into this sea of ​​people without even a splash.

He took a rough look around and made an estimate in his mind.

At least, there are five thousand.

There are people wearing brocade, followed by servants holding boxes.

Some were wearing coarse cloth and had patched bundles slung over their shoulders.

There are those who are fourteen or fifteen years old and still have childish faces, and there are also those who are in their early twenties and have stubble on their chins.

People from all over the world and from all walks of life crowded into this square today.

In front of the square, there were about ten senior brothers in blue robes, who were busy maintaining order on the scene.

The robe was more exquisite than the one taught by Professor Jin. It was made of fine fine cloth, with a small leaf embroidered on the left chest. The stitching was so fine that even the veins of the leaf were clearly defined.

The leader, the senior brother, looked about sixteen or seventeen years old. He looked at the thick heads below and said in a low voice:

"This year there are more than 5,000 people."

The older senior brother next to him said "hmm" and didn't take it to heart.

He has seen this situation three times, and it happens every spring.

There were 5,000 faces when we entered, but after half a year there were no longer enough 500 people to stay.

He glanced at the people in the crowd who were hunching their necks and holding their old baggage, and then at the people who were surrounded by servants...

The indescribable feeling in my heart flashed through me.

Who is the loach and who is the dragon?

Can't tell at this time.

Every senior brother has a parrot on his shoulder.

Parrots are much larger than the average parrot.

The whole body feathers are bright peacock blue, and the tail feathers are very long.

There is also a thin circle of gold lines on the side of the beak, which will glow when the sun shines.

The senior brother at the head was not loud.

He just said lightly, "To the east, stand thirty rows in," but this sentence suddenly expanded tenfold and spread clearly to every corner of the square.

The most interesting thing is that thousands of heads are crowded together...

Under normal circumstances, it should be as noisy as going to a market.

But the humming human voice was suppressed very low at this time, making the senior brother's words even clearer.

Luo Ying knew this kind of bird.

[Noisy Parrot], the evolved form of [Calling Parrot].

When he went to the market last year, he saw one in front of the largest animal stall in town.

At that time, the bird was standing on the shopkeeper's shoulder, shouting at the top of his voice, and his cry could be heard throughout the street.

Luo Ying watched from a distance for a long time and heard the old man selling vegetables next to him muttering:

"This bird's gold is very expensive. No matter how low the awakening level is, it still costs more than ten taels of silver."

Ordinary farmers would not dare to think about it, so only big businessmen are willing to raise one to show off their wealth.

A dozen taels.

Luo Ying touched his sleeve unconsciously.

There was nothing inside the sleeves, it was very empty.

But he also felt that the place was heavy.

Lao Hei's pair of corners totaled six taels.

A cow had been feeding for fifteen years and bumped into a stone pillar countless times in the middle of the night before taking off six taels of food from its head.

And in this square, the bird on senior brother's shoulder alone is worth more than the opposite corner of Lao Hei, and there is still a small margin.

There are about ten such birds standing here.

Just to get people to line up.

Luo Ying was not jealous, nor could he become red.

He just felt that the blue bricks under his feet and the blue bricks under the feet of those senior brothers were obviously in the same square, but there seemed to be an invisible river between them.

The senior brothers directed the flow of people, row by row, to the pavilion at the end of the square.

The attic is not big.

The walls are made of blue bricks and the roof is covered with black tiles. The facade is not as grand as the main entrance of the academy. It seems a bit inconspicuous in such a large square.

Luo Ying murmured in his heart.

How could five thousand people squeeze into such an ordinary-sized pavilion?

But the people at the front walked in one by one, just like mud cows entering the sea. As many as they went in, they were packed inside silently, and there was no congestion at the door.

It's Luo Ying's turn.

Li Zicheng stood next to him, shoulder to shoulder, and moved toward the door with the flow of people.

"Stay closer."

Li Zicheng lowered his voice:

"There are many people, don't disperse."
